review_candidates.title: Director of Finance
review_candidates.description: About Us: Founded in 1989, the Asian American Federation (AAF) is one of the strongest leadership voices advocating for better policies, services, and funding that lead to more justice and opportunity for Asian immigrants, one of the most historically under-resourced  communities in New York City. As an umbrella leadership organization, we represent 70 community-based organizations serving 1.5 million Asian New Yorkers, the fastest-growing population in the city. Our Core Values: Our employees, interns, and volunteers are expected to embody AAF's core values: Leading With Integrity Purposeful Transparency Committed to Accountability Guided By Our Community The Opportunity AAF is seeking an experienced Director of Finance (DoF) to lead the organization's financial operations, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and compliance functions. Reporting to the COO and managing the Finance Team, the DoF will serve as a key thought partner to senior leadership, ensuring strong financial stewardship while developing systems and processes that support AAF's continued growth and impact.  The ideal candidate brings strong nonprofit accounting expertise, with the ability to translate financial information into actionable insights for organizational leaders. This individual will be a hands-on, collaborative leader with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, actionable insights for organizational leaders. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable overseeing day-to-day financial operations and contributing to long-term financial planning and strategy.  Major responsibilities will include, but not exclusive to the following : Strategic Partnership & Leadership Serve as a primary advisor to the COO and executive leadership, delivering financial modeling, risk analysis, and scenario projections and forecasting to guide strategy to support organizational planning, resource allocation, revenue strategy, and decision-making. Develop financial models, scenario analyses, and projections to evaluate strategic initiatives, new programs, funding opportunities, organizational growth, and other significant business decisions. Partner with senior leadership and program teams to assess the financial implications and sustainability of new programs, contracts, partnerships, and organizational initiatives, including funding requirements, staffing, cost structures, cash-flow implications, organizational capacity, and financial risk. Present clear financial performance metrics, cash-flow analysis, financial trends, opportunities, and strategic insights to senior leadership, the Board of Directors, and relevant committees into clear, actionable recommendations. Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Planning Lead the annual organizational budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning process, providing department heads with regular budget-to-actual reporting, revenue monitoring, and variance analysis throughout the year and partnering to develop realistic programs and team budgets. Manage the annual audit process and coordinate required tax, regulatory, compliance, and financial filings alongside external auditors and legal advisors. Manage organizational cash flow and liquidity, including short- and long-term cash forecasting, accounts receivable and reimbursement timing, and liquidity planning to ensure AAF can meet its operating and programmatic obligations. Accounting Operations & Financial and Systems Controls Oversee the integrity of the general ledger and key accounting functions, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, reconciliations, cash management, and month- and year-end close processes, ensuring complete, accurate, and timely financial records - ensuring strict GAAP compliance. Establish, strengthen, and maintain robust internal controls, financial policies and practices, segregation of duties, and data security protocols to safeguard organizational assets and to improve forecasting accuracy, accountability, and visibility into the organization’s current and projected financial position. Evaluate and modernize accounting, budgeting, and grant-management technology to enhance reporting capabilities, data integrity, and cross-departmental efficiency. Grants, Contracts & Restricted Funding Oversee financial management for grants, gifts, and contracts, ensuring accurate revenue recognition, donor-restricted fund tracking, cost allocations, and funder compliance. Partner with Development and program leadership to review the financial components of prospective and awarded grants and contracts, including proposed budgets, funding restrictions, direct and indirect costs, cost-allocation methodologies, reporting requirements, reimbursement structures, and cash-flow implications. Assess the financial feasibility and organizational capacity associated with funding opportunities and help ensure AAF can meet financial, operational, reporting, and compliance obligations before and throughout the funding period. Monitor grant and contract financial performance and collaborate with program and Development teams to identify and address budget variances, reimbursement delays, funding gaps, compliance concerns, and other financial risks. Team Management & Board Collaboration Supervise finance staff and/or consultants as the team grows and build the capacity of the team through ongoing training and development. Establish clear performance expectations, operational workflows, and growth opportunities. Partner with the Board Treasurer and relevant Board committees on financial oversight and governance, including collaborating with the Treasurer on the annual budgeting process and ongoing financial performance; supporting the Audit Committee in its oversight of the annual audit and related financial matters; and working with the Investment Committee to support oversight and monitoring of AAF’s investment portfolio in accordance with Board-approved policies and organizational objectives. Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned in support of AAF’s mission and organizational priorities. Candidate Profile The ideal candidate will have most, if not all, of the following professional and personal qualities, skills, and characteristics: A Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance,  or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. CPA or advanced degree is a plus; 7+ years of progressively responsible accounting and finance experience, including significant experience in nonprofit financial management; demonstrating expertise in nonprofit accounting, including restricted and unrestricted funding, grant accounting, cost allocation, and government and private funding sources; 4+ years of experience managing nonprofit financial operations and supervising staff; Extensive Experience with New York City and/or New York State government contracts, reimbursement requirements, cost allocation, and compliance is strongly preferred; Proficiency with QuickBooks Online or comparable accounting systems, with demonstrated ability to improve financial systems, reporting, and workflows; Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret financial information and communicate key findings to both financial and non-financial stakeholders;  Exceptional attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines;  Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with the ability to work effectively across departments and with a diverse team; and  Commitment to AAF’s mission, values, and work in support of Asian American communities.  Compensation & Benefits This position is based in New York City, with a hybrid work environment. The salary range for this position is $126,000 to $134,000, commensurate with experience. To uphold organizational parity and pay equity, AAF will use a non-negotiable salary structure that takes into consideration the entire breadth of a candidate’s experience, employment, and education to arrive at their base salary. In addition, AAF provides a comprehensive benefits package that includes 100% employee health care, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; commuter benefits, as well as a 403(b) plan with up to 3% employer match and generous paid time off. To Apply :  Please email cover letter, resume, and writing sample with [Last Name] Director of Finance in the subject line to HR@aafederation.org . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position will begin immediately. No phone calls, please. The Asian American Federation is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

review_candidates.title: Assistant Manager (Experience Design)
review_candidates.description: National Gallery Singapore is looking for a curious, hands-on Product Designer to help shape how visitors discover, navigate and engage with the Gallery and its art. The role requires close collaboration across the organisation to understand visitor needs through both qualitative and quantitative data, frame the right problems, explore possibilities, and test ideas before significant investment is made. This is primarily a digital product-design role. You will design and improve visitor-facing products and services across the Gallery’s digital ecosystem, spanning visit planning, ticketing, on-site interpretation and post-visit engagement. You will also contribute UX research and design expertise to selected spatial initiatives, including visitor orientation, wayfinding, and gallery spatial blueprinting. You might prototype a new online visit-planning journey, test how visitors navigate a Gallery space, develop reusable digital interface patterns, or translate research and operational data into a clear product roadmap. We are looking for someone who combines strong UI and UX craft with human-centred research, systems thinking and rapid prototyping. You should be comfortable moving between ambiguity and detail, from defining problems with stakeholders to building and testing tangible solutions. You do not need to come from a museum, but you should be interested in art, culture and the ways museums can become more delightful, welcoming, accessible, and engaging for different audiences. What you will do Design digital products and visitor experiences Design intuitive and inclusive digital experiences across the visitor journey. Translate visitor needs, organisational priorities, and operational constraints into information architectures, user flows, wireframes, interfaces and testable prototypes. Carry work from early discovery and concept development through validation, design specification, implementation support and post-launch improvement. Work closely with technology teams and delivery partners to ensure that the implemented experience reflects the intended interaction and visual design. Apply accessibility and inclusive-design principles so that products work for visitors with different abilities, languages, levels of digital confidence and familiarity with museums. Maintain a high standard of interaction and visual-design craft while balancing usability, feasibility, maintainability and delivery constraints. Apply UX research and design methods to selected spatial experiences, such as visitor orientation / wayfinding, spatial blueprinting, and movement through the Gallery. Map, prototype, and test spatial journeys and concepts, translating findings into clear visitor-experience requirements for internal teams and delivery partners. Research, frame and validate Work with visitors, frontline colleagues and internal teams to uncover needs, behaviours, pain points, and opportunities. Plan and conduct appropriate research, including contextual observation, interviews, journey mapping, co-design, concept testing, and usability testing. Synthesise qualitative and quantitative evidence into clear insights, opportunity areas, and actionable design recommendations. Turn ambiguous requests into well-defined problem statements, design hypotheses, and measurable outcomes. Prototype early and at the appropriate level of fidelity to test assumptions before solutions are commissioned or built. Establish feedback and evaluation loops so that products can improve after launch. Steward the Gallery’s digital design system Serve as the steward of the Gallery’s digital design system for visitor-facing products and services. Develop and maintain reusable components, interaction patterns, accessibility requirements and practical design guidance. Work with brand, content, digital and technology colleagues to ensure that the system reflects the Gallery’s identity and can be implemented consistently. Maintain clear documentation that internal teams and external delivery partners can apply. Review designs produced by project teams and vendors, providing constructive guidance on consistency, usability and accessibility. Identify gaps and evolve the system based on emerging product needs, implementation realities and visitor feedback. Turn evidence into product direction Work with visitor/ stakeholder feedback, behavioural data, analytics and operational information to identify patterns and prioritise opportunities. Translate insights into prototypes, product requirements, experience specifications and phased roadmaps. Define success measures with project teams and assess whether interventions have improved visitor outcomes. Communicate the rationale behind design decisions through visual storytelling, demonstrations and concise documentation. Balance visitor desirability with technical feasibility, operational sustainability, cost and long-term maintainability. Collaborate across the Gallery Partner and collaborate with teams across the gallery. Facilitate workshops, design critiques, and working sessions that help teams align around visitor needs and make informed decisions. Work with consultants, technology partners, and design vendors to frame briefs, review proposals and maintain design quality throughout delivery. Provide clear specifications and feedback while remaining open to technical content and operational perspectives. Help teams build confidence in human-centred design through practical tools, methods and examples. Support museum innovation and AI initiatives Contribute design and research expertise to visitor-centred innovation and responsible AI initiatives. Explore how AI and other emerging technologies could improve access to art, personalisation, orientation, learning and operational effectiveness. Build lightweight prototypes to make emerging possibilities tangible and testable. Consider privacy, accessibility, intellectual property, bias, transparency and long-term maintainability when designing AI-enabled experiences. Requirements At least 3-5 years of relevant professional experience in product design, UI/UX design, user research, design consulting, product management, or a related field. A portfolio of UI, UX, or product-design work that demonstrates your thinking, process, craft and contribution, not only finished screens. Strong foundations in interaction design, information architecture, prototyping and visual interface design. Experience applying human-centred design methods to understand users, test assumptions and improve solutions. The ability to create prototypes ranging from quick sketches and clickable flows to detailed, high-fidelity experiences. Proficiency with contemporary design and prototyping tools, particularly Figma, and experience in AI-enabled design and prototyping (Make, Codex, Claude Code, etc.). The ability to interpret research findings and data and turn them into clear design decisions. Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain design decisions and engage effectively with diverse stakeholders. A collaborative, resourceful and hands-on approach, with the ability to manage multiple streams of work. Comfort working in open or ambiguous problem spaces and the judgement to bring structure, momentum and clarity. It would be an added advantage if you have Strong practical experience using AI in your daily design practice - for research synthesis, ideation, prototyping, content exploration, coding or workflow improvement. Experience in museums, galleries, arts, culture, heritage, attractions or other public-facing environments.

review_candidates.title: Area adviser
review_candidates.description: Company Description Wendi Foundation is a Uganda-based non-profit organization focused on empowering individuals to drive sustainable community and national development. Since 2013, Wendi has advanced education, skills development, and leadership initiatives to help people become effective change-makers and nation-builders. The foundation delivers vocational training, mentorship, and community engagement programs that address local challenges and promote social cohesion. Wendi also advocates for policies and initiatives that expand opportunities for individuals to contribute to a more prosperous, equitable, and sustainable society. Team members join a mission-driven organization that invests in people and long-term impact. Role Description The Area Adviser is a full-time remote role responsible for supporting Wendi’s programs and initiatives across designated regions. This role involves providing strategic guidance to local partners, monitoring project implementation, and ensuring that activities align with Wendi’s mission and standards. The Area Adviser will coordinate with community leaders, stakeholders, and internal teams to identify needs, design practical solutions, and track progress toward development goals. Day-to-day tasks include collecting and analyzing field data, preparing reports and recommendations, facilitating virtual meetings and trainings, and sharing best practices to strengthen leadership and empowerment efforts. The role also requires active collaboration with program staff to improve outreach, enhance community engagement, and support advocacy activities. Qualifications Experience in community development, social work, or related fields, with strong skills in stakeholder engagement and relationship building. Competence in project coordination and monitoring, including planning, data collection, documentation, and reporting. Ability to provide advisory support, conduct needs assessments, and develop practical recommendations for program improvement. Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, including the ability to facilitate virtual meetings, trainings, and presentations. Knowledge of leadership development, empowerment approaches, and grassroots advocacy in a non-profit or mission-driven context. Comfort with remote work tools and digital collaboration platforms; ability to work independently across time zones and communities. Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, Education, Management, or a related field is preferred. Prior experience working in or with communities in Uganda or similar contexts is an advantage.
